summary: Make `board` the orchestrating capability. Its application layer owns board policy and projection; work-items and labels remain independent persistence-owning capabilities accessed only through trusted server surfaces. The App Router page consumes a board-specific RSC surface.

tree.purpose: RSC route; authenticates the request, invokes `board/rsc.ts`, and renders loading, expected failure, or grouped board data.
Framework-neutral orchestration: loads work-items and referenced labels, hides archived items, groups by status, attaches label details, and rejects inaccessible labels.
Small board-owned ports for reading board work-items and visible labels without depending on provider implementations.
Pure board projection types and grouping/attachment invariants.
Adapter calling `src/modules/work-items/server.ts`; maps work-item results into the board port.
Adapter calling `src/modules/labels/server.ts`; requests labels for the actor and reports inaccessible or missing referenced labels.
Server-only dependency wiring, request identity propagation, and provider/error mapping.
Server-only current-request API used by the page; authenticates/authorizes, invokes the application operation, and returns the board projection or typed expected failure.
Existing trusted server API owned by work-items; exposes actor-scoped reads and work-item persistence.
Existing trusted server API owned by labels; exposes actor-scoped visible-label reads and label persistence.

flows: `app/(product)/board/page.tsx` → `board/rsc.ts` → authenticate request and construct request identity → `board/application/load-board.ts`.
The board operation calls the work-items port first, because label IDs come from the returned work-items. Archived items are filtered before label lookup.
`board/server/work-items-reader.ts` → `work-items/server.ts`; the actor, tenant/ownership scope, request ID, and trace ID are propagated.
The operation collects referenced label IDs and calls `board/server/labels-reader.ts` → `labels/server.ts` once for the set of IDs.
If every referenced label is visible, the operation attaches label details and groups remaining items by status.
If any referenced label is not visible or is absent, the operation returns `LabelAccessDenied`/`LabelReferenceInvalid`; it does not silently omit the label or render a partial board.
`board/rsc.ts` maps expected outcomes to page data or an inline error state. Unexpected defects are reported once at the RSC boundary and allowed to follow framework error handling.

decisions.rationale: Filtering archived items, label-access policy, attachment, grouping, and coordination are board-specific policy that should survive removal of Next.js routes.

decisions.choice: Board depends on work-items and labels only through `server.ts` public surfaces
decisions.rationale: The capabilities remain independently changeable, have no mutual imports, and the module graph stays acyclic.

decisions.choice: Expose only `board/rsc.ts` for this read path; retain `work-items/server.ts` and `labels/server.ts` as trusted server APIs
decisions.rationale: No Server Action, browser read, HTTP endpoint, stream, or job is required by the task.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at `board/rsc.ts`; enforce board policy in the application; enforce tenant/ownership predicates in each capability store boundary
decisions.rationale: Each boundary handles the authorization concern appropriate to its layer while preserving actor scope downstream.

decisions.choice: Typed expected failures for inaccessible labels, invalid references, and dependency outages; exceptions for unexpected defects
decisions.rationale: The RSC page can render intentional failure states without conflating them with programming or infrastructure defects.

decisions.choice: Keep the initial board read request-scoped; add cache metadata only if caching is later introduced
decisions.rationale: The task requires actor-dependent visibility, so shared caching would risk leaking authorization-sensitive data.

decisions.choice: Outcome-focused unit, contract, integration, and route tests
decisions.rationale: Tests should verify policy and failure/report-once behavior rather than internal call counts.

risks: A label becoming inaccessible between the work-item and label reads can make the board fail atomically; this is intentional under the reject-on-inaccessible-label requirement.
Actor-dependent data must not use a shared cache key unless actor, tenant, and authorization scope are included and validated.
Production checks should enforce `server-only` boundaries and fail if client code imports `board/rsc.ts`, `work-items/server.ts`, `labels/server.ts`, or `src/**/server/**`.
